blocks.x: Retail media incrementality proven, clean-room measurement adopted by every major brand

A national consumer-electronics chain: a Retail & Consumer Goods program run on the outcome-linked model with a blended Achala IT Solutions team. The name stays behind the NDA; the numbers are published with permission.
Vendor claims rested on last-touch logic; the retailer could not arbitrate.
Peak-season cloud costs discovered on invoices; P95 cost per order unknown. Personalization stalled on privacy-office veto.

We built the clean-room measurement service (joint retailer-brand testing without data leakage), engineered peak readiness with load/chaos discipline and unit-cost telemetry, and shipped privacy-architected personalization, consent-scoped profiling with clean-room verification. Brands now buy measured incrementality, not impressions.

blocks.x: The three things that made it hold

items: lineage and freshness were design constraints from week one, so the measurement never became the controversy.
unit economics were visible from the first workload, so the run-rate never surprised anyone.
the models and retrieval systems were evaluated before anyone trusted them, grounded answers, cited sources, measured quality.

blocks.x: Two things from the national consumer-electronics chain program generalize, the governance shape and the gate design. Everything else was estate-specific, and pretending otherwise is how programs waste their first quarter The engagement model here was build-run; the same pattern runs fixed-scope where the estate allows it.
